title: The Garlock Fault
text: Johannesburg is one of the communities closest to the Garlock Fault, which is about 250 kilometers, or 160 miles, long. The two sides of the fault slide past each other horizontally, in what geologists call left-lateral motion. The last significant surface ruptures are thought to have come about 1050 A.D. near Tehachapi and about 1500 A.D. near Johannesburg. No earthquake has produced surface rupture on the Garlock Fault in historic times, though a magnitude 5.7 earthquake occurred in 1992. The fault is named for the mining town of Garlock, founded in 1894 by Eugene Garlock and now a ghost town.
